about: Every scope, claim, gate and refusal reason a vits.me relying party can use. Source of truth for omniauth-vitsme (OmniAuth::Vitsme::Catalog) and for agents and developers choosing scopes. Mirrors the vits.me server: config/initializers/doorkeeper.rb (scopes), config/initializers/doorkeeper_openid_connect.rb (claims), config/initializers/authorizations_controller_extension.rb (value domains, gates, refusals).

conventions.delivery: Every claim except sub comes from the UserInfo endpoint, never the ID token; the one exception is a trip's ticket, vitsme_trip, which only the ID token carries (see trips). omniauth-vitsme fetches UserInfo on every sign-in.
conventions.sign_in_and_ask: A sign-in names nobody and asks only identity scopes (openid, fluid) and gates. An ask names the person it is about, the person signed in to your app (ask_about:), and may ask for details. vits.me refuses a request for details that names nobody (subject_required), and omniauth-vitsme refuses one at boot.
conventions.absent_means_undisclosed: A disclosure claim may be missing even when its scope was granted: the person chose to share nothing, holds no such detail, or hid it. Missing is never false.
conventions.required_scopes: In an ask, a star after a detail scope marks it required: full_name__intl*, and email* at a partner. The consent page marks it and waits until the person gives it; the person may still cancel (access_denied). Only a detail may be required: a star on openid, fluid or a gate is refused (invalid_scope), and so is a starred scope the server does not answer. Registrations, claims and the token's scope carry plain names. omniauth-vitsme checks the answer too, and fails required_missing for one without a required claim.
conventions.person_chooses_the_value: For disclosure claims the person picks the value on vits.me's consent screen, from options at different levels of detail (e.g. a given name, initials, or a full name). Ask for the least you need.
conventions.sub_is_private: sub, solid, defunct_solids and fluid are private per-site identifiers. Store them; never render, log, put in a URL, federate or derive a public handle or email from them.

fluid.description: Also sign in people whose verification is still pending (sub = fluid_...). Cannot be combined with a nationality gate.

sub.format: solid_<base32> for a verified person; fluid_<base32> for a pending signup (only with the fluid scope)
sub.description: Pairwise subject: the same person has a different sub at every site. The OmniAuth uid.

solid.description: Equal to sub for a verified person; absent for a pending signup.

defunct_solids.description: Earlier SOLIDs this site was given for the same person (kept one year). If your record holds one of these, move it to the current sub.

fluid.description: Pending-signup identifiers this site may have been given for the same person in the past week. Merge any tentative account keyed by one into this person.

name.description: One name, at the level of detail the person chose. Not split into given and family names. May be in Hebrew script.

name__full.description: A full name, chosen from the person's full-name forms, in either script. Deprecated: ask for full_name__intl (the default) or full_name__local. vits.me still answers it for a site that holds it, and offers it to no new registration.

full_name__local.description: A full name in the person's own language and script: Hebrew for an Israeli. The person may leave out given names or show them as initials, keeping at least one written out; the family name is whole. Not a legal name.

full_name__intl.format: Latin letters A-Z, words joined by a space, a dash or an apostrophe, and a period only after an initial; capitalized, never all caps; no accents
full_name__intl.description: A full name in its international variant: the English version, capitalized, in Latin letters without accents. The person may leave out given names or show them as initials, keeping at least one written out; the family name is whole. Not a legal name.

nationality.description: A nationality the person holds and chose to share.

nationality__in_eu.description: Whether the shared nationality is an EU member state.

nationality__in_eea.description: Whether the shared nationality is in the European Economic Area.

nationality__in_esm.description: Whether the shared nationality is in the European Single Market.

nationality__gdpr_compliant.description: Whether the shared nationality is an EEA member state or the United Kingdom.

il_government_id_number.description: Israeli government ID number (teudat zehut). Highly sensitive: request only with a legal need.

portrait.format: An object: content_type "image/jpeg", width and height in pixels, and content, the JPEG in standard base64 (RFC 4648 §4, no line breaks). Always a plain sRGB JPEG with no metadata, at most 200 KB, at the passport's own resolution and framing (about 7:9), never cropped or upscaled.
portrait.description: The person's photo: the face their passport chip carries, the one they chose to share. Sent whole: keep your own copy, there is no URL to fetch it from. Enabled by vits.me on request, per site, since a face links a person's accounts across sites whatever their identifiers.

age.description: The person's age at the level they chose: a threshold, a generation, a range, or exact years.

age__over_13.description: Whether the person is 13 or older.

age__over_18.description: Whether the person is 18 or older.

age__over_21.description: Whether the person is 21 or older.

birthday.format: M-D (month-day, no year) or YYYY-MM-DD, as the person chose
birthday.description: Birthday. The person may share it with or without the year.

openid_nationality.description: Only verified people holding one of the requested nationalities can finish signing in. Several codes are any-of. Emits no claim: a successful sign-in is the answer. vits.me asks the person's consent for the verdict. Refused people return with error=access_denied and vitsme_error=nationality_gate (or nationality_gate_unverified).

knots.description: Claims from a partner service (a KNOT) that verifies what vits.me does not. Partners are OAuth servers of their own, asked directly with the vitsme_partner strategy, never through vits.me: none is listed here. GET <issuer>/knot/partners lists them with their status; only an active one is asked or believed (OmniAuth::Vitsme::Partner.listing). Each documents its own scopes.
knots.auth_hash: uid is the partner's own identifier for the person at your site; extra.claims holds its answer, an empty list for a scope not given; credentials.refresh_token when it keeps a standing consent.
knots.fresh_claims: While the standing consent holds: OmniAuth::Vitsme::Partner.fresh_claims(partner:, client_id:, partner_secret:, refresh_token:, vitsme_issuer:). Raises Refused once it does not.
knots.events: Register an events address with the partner; verify each POST with OmniAuth::Vitsme::Events.verify!(token, partner:, client_id:) (claims_changed, consent_withdrawn) and answer 202.

trips.description: Several asks from one button under one pincode: vits.me first, then each partner the site names as a stop, each on its own page. The vitsme_trip strategy runs one. The first ask is pushed with vitsme_stops (the partners' issuers, space-separated, at most 4, each active and named once) and names its subject; the pincode page names every stop. The ID token of that ask carries vitsme_trip, the trip's ticket; sealed for each partner as its subject, it lets vits.me answer that partner's sign-in without the pincode page, once, for the same person, site and browser, within 10 minutes and the first stop within 2. Anything else is the pincode page again, never an error.

nationality_gate.description: The person holds none of the nationalities the gate requires (or has hidden them).

nationality_gate_unverified.description: A pending (unverified) signup tried to pass a nationality gate.

subject_mismatch.description: The ask named its person (claims sub value) and a different person is signed in at vits.me.

subject_required.description: The request asked for details and named nobody. Ask about the person signed in to your app (ask_about:); a sign-in asks only openid and gates. Refused before the pincode.

stops_invalid.description: A trip named stops vits.me cannot take: a partner it does not list as active, one named twice, more than four, or stops on a request that does not name its person. Refused at the push, before the pincode.

subject_invalid.description: A partner carried a sealed subject vits.me cannot read: not an ID token vits.me issued, for a site that is gone, or naming nobody. Partners see it; the site hears from the partner that the person was not asked.

application_suspended.description: vits.me has suspended this site. Nobody can sign in to it until the suspension is lifted; its owner sees why on the site's page in the developer area.
